newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down one pct on wait for new govt.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down one pct on wait for new govt.

text.p: Thai stocks retreated for the second day on Tuesday, losing one percent as investors sold shares amid uncertainty over the shape of a new cabinet being formed by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, brokers said.
The SET index finished 9.63 points lower at 958.14 on about four billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index slipped 0.95 point to 73.42.
"Investors adopted a wait-and-see attitude and decided to sell while they waited for a new government. Foreigners would likely remain net sellers today," said Lan Pajasalmi of First Asia Securities.
Net foreign selling in the Thai bourse amounted to 777 million baht on Monday.
Chavalit and his new cabinet are expected to be sworn in by King Bhumibol Adulyadej on December 1.
All major counters declined with the machinery and equipment sector taking the heaviest blow, losing 2.3 percent. The communications sector fell 1.9 percent.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling 1.50 baht to 77.50, National Finance dipped 1.50 to 65, Siam Cement declined 24 to 872, and TelecomAsia retreated 1.50 to 54.50.
Brokers expect the market to find support at about 940 and resistance at 980 on Wednesday.
